newsitem.title: UK: United says British open sky demands obstructive.
newsitem.headline: United says British open sky demands obstructive.

text.p: United Airlines said Thursday that British airline demands to be allowed to operate domestic U.S. routes were blocking the way to getting an Anglo-U.S. open skies aviation pact and should be dropped as being immaterial.

Speaking to an American Chamber of Commerce lunch Chairman Gerald Greenwald said in terms of commercial value the demands really amounted to only "1 percent of the business issue" and suggested that the demand was being made by Richard Branson's Virgin Atlantic only to prevent a deal being done.
"I think those who are saying that are saying we don't want a deal at all,'" Greenwald said.
Failure to agree an open skies pact would block the proposed alliance between Virgin's arch rival British Airways and American Airlines.
Virgin has been a vociferous opponent of the controversial pact, complaining that it would dominate the British trans-Atlantic market with more than 60 percent of all flights.

Under the alliance, British Airways intends to coordinate its 244 flights a week from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with all of American's 238 flights a week from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.
British Airways and American argue their deal will lead to greater competition because it will only go ahead if Britain and the U.S. agree to establish an "open skies" free market.
